analysis:
This batch contains only documentation and a changelog: changelog.d/selected-models-recover.md (new), docs/architecture/addon-hold.md (invariant 5, lines 66-71 head) and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (new selected-model recovery section, head lines 371-408). No executable code is included, so no code-level regression can be verified here. The implementation (ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift, enterAddonHold, isProtectedFromRecoveryEviction, selectedModelRecoveryVictimWait) is not supplied.

Security-relevant behavior the docs describe, which the next pass should check against source if it is available:
- TB-012/T-059/A-018: selected-model recovery is refused or deferred while an add-on hold is active, and a hold that begins mid-attempt cancels the recovery load (enterAddonHold). The docs are consistent with the hold load fence (addonHoldLoadRefusal). Whether the new recovery load path actually checks that fence is unverified. A bypass would load models beside add-on VMs.
- Recovery evicts non-selected resident models before the load's own checks, so a load that then fails can have evicted victims. The docs state that this is bounded to one attempt per model. This is an availability concern (A-018, T-029/T-010 class) and is documented as accepted, not an observed flaw.
- The changelog describes a pending owner-review policy that releases adopted non-selected models. It is flagged as not yet approved. It is not in the docs diff, so it is unverifiable here.
- The 15 s shutdown unload timeout means a model's native retirement may not finish before process exit. Consider the effect on T-028 (residual GPU memory) and on unload/KV-release guarantees.

No threat assumption is invalidated by the documentation change. The threat model's TB-012 and T-059 text may need a mention of the recovery path as a new load initiator if it is implemented as described. Marking deeper review because the code is not supplied.
